title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a preregistered, paired experiment (N=120 intent→configuration tasks) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) against an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). A single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) produced one shared initial candidate per paired task (model_calls_used = 120); the guarded pipeline would invoke at most one repair iteration only when the deterministic emulator validator reported violations. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120 = 1.00; guarded success = 120/120 = 1.00 (contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes (no validator-detected violations occurred). Contamination checks reported none. Key archived artifact filenames (full manifest archived): preregistration (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1), execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We incorporate reviewer-requested clarifications grounded in archived execution artifacts (shared-initial-generation semantics and repair-trigger logic) and discuss the observed ceiling effect, the design tradeoffs introduced by the shared-generation choice, and the external-validity limitations of this synthetic, deterministic harness.

sections.introduction: Automating configuration tasks with generative LLMs can speed NetOps but creates operational risk: syntactically plausible commands may violate workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break, required shutdown sequences) and produce semantic regressions. Prior work therefore proposes tool-augmented architectures—generate→validate→repair loops, veto layers, or digital twins—that run generated candidates in a verifier or emulator before enactment. We test a focused question derived from that literature: Does inserting an executable emulator-based validator into a generate→validate→repair loop reduce semantic (network-level) failures of LLM-generated configuration changes compared with an LLM-only suggestion workflow? We preregistered study CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1, implemented a deterministic emulator validator and deterministic task generator, and executed a paired experiment over N=120 tasks using a single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini). Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, deterministic paired experiment that isolates validator/repair effects by using a single shared initial generation per paired task; (2) artifact-grounded clarifications requested by peer review (shared-generation semantics, repair-trigger logic, and minimal artifact-hash disclosure); and (3) a transparent analysis and interpretation of a narrow null/ceiling result together with operational implications and reproducibility pointers.
sections.related_work: Prior surveys and benchmarks demonstrate that syntactic evaluation of LLM outputs misses operational failure modes and that verifier- or emulator-augmented workflows can detect semantic errors (e.g., executable benchmark efforts and generate→validate→repair tool chains). Representative recent work shows simulator- or verifier-backed evaluations exposing failures in closed-loop NetOps tasks and advocates guardrails (veto layers, canaries, digital twins) for safety. These studies motivate our confirmatory design: rather than a multi-model leaderboard, we provide a preregistered, artifact-backed paired test focused on whether an executable validator materially changes semantic outcomes when the same LLM candidate is shared across conditions. (Representative nearest works are cited in the bibliography.)
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study followed a preregistered paired binary design (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1). Exactly N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks were deterministically generated and assigned into three topology classes (40 tasks each: edge, core, leaf–spine) per the preregistration. For each task we produced one shared initial candidate from gpt-5-mini (initial_generation_calls_per_task=1; independent_condition_generation=false) and evaluated that candidate in two conditions: baseline (LLM-only suggestion applied to emulator) and guarded (same candidate subjected to generate→validate→repair; repair budget ≤1 iteration and only attempted if validator reported violations). Primary estimand and test: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline tested with exact two-sided McNemar (alpha=0.05). Confidence interval: bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729). Model and prompting: all candidate configurations came from gpt-5-mini under a frozen prompt/config (see execution/model_configuration.json in the archived manifest). Execution and validator: a deterministic emulator-based validator performed intent-constraint and workflow-policy checks (examples: make-before-break, required shutdown→change→restore). Inclusion/exclusion: technical/instrumentation failures would be excluded per preregistration; none occurred. Minimal artifact disclosure (filenames only; full manifest archived): preregistration manifest (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1), execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. Shared-generation accounting: the run used a single shared-initial-generation per paired task, explaining model_calls_used = 120 despite a planned maximum_model_calls = 240. Repair-trigger logic: guarded repairs were conditional on validator-detected violation_count>0; archived validator traces show repair_applied = false for every guarded episode (no repairs invoked). Validator-coverage and task-difficulty summary: the deterministic validator reported zero violations across all 240 episodes (validator_violation_count = 0 for every scoring JSON entry archived under execution/scoring/). Contamination checks: analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (no flags). Representative task-difficulty sample from the archived task_manifest (n=6 representative entries included in the evidence bundle) shows difficulty.level ∈ {medium:1, hard:2, very_hard:3}; the full task_manifest (N=120) is archived for inspection but a global difficulty histogram is not summarized inline here. Example (representative) validator normalized configuration (from execution/scoring/task-000001): "interface edge1 admin down; interface edge1 vlan 30; interface edge1 mtu 1600; interface edge1 admin up."
sections.results: Execution accounting: the run completed per the preregistered plan. Episodes and calls: 240 episodes (120 pairs) completed; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared initial generation per task). Validator scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 reported each candidate valid; contingency counts: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Observed success rates: baseline = 120/120 = 1.00; guarded = 120/120 = 1.00. Confirmatory analysis: paired-difference estimate = 0.00; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Repair activity: in guarded episodes, repair_applied = false for all tasks (emulator reported violation_count = 0 on every initial candidate), so no repair iterations occurred and preregistered secondary metrics (tasks requiring repair, mean repair calls) are vacuous here. Missingness and contamination: no episodes were excluded; contamination_summary.csv contains no flags. Artifacts and reproducibility: full raw responses, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts are archived per the preregistration manifest.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and ceiling effect: the confirmatory outcome is a narrow null—on this curated synthetic task set, with a single model and a frozen prompt and with a deterministic validator, the guarded loop provided no additional reduction in semantic failures because the baseline already produced emulator-valid outputs for every task. Consequence for preregistered power: the preregistration targeted an absolute reduction of 0.15 (15 percentage points) and planned power (≈80%) under plausible baseline failure ≈0.40; the observed baseline=1.00 violates these assumptions and produces a ceiling that renders the McNemar test uninformative for the preregistered effect size. Design tradeoffs: the shared-initial-generation design intentionally isolates validator/repair efficacy from generation variance (it avoids conflating model-generation randomness with repair effects) but also prevents detection of generation-induced discordance between conditions; had independent per-condition generations been used, the guarded pipeline could have been credited for repairing discordant, invalid baseline generations. Validator coverage and external validity: the deterministic emulator detected zero violations for the shared candidates; this may reflect (a) relatively constrained synthetic tasks that the model handled well, (b) validator fidelity that matches those task templates, or (c) both. The archived task_manifest, scoring traces, and full execution manifest permit further inspection; nonetheless, external generalization to noisy, adversarial, multi-vendor production environments remains limited. Operational implication: a guarded generate→validate→repair architecture remains a recommended safety design in heterogeneous or adversarial settings—our result shows only that under these tightly controlled conditions the guarded loop did not change semantic outcomes. Follow-up experiments should (i) evaluate independent per-condition generation, (ii) include multiple models and prompt variants, (iii) expand repair budgets and richer repair strategies, and (iv) use higher-fidelity or multi-vendor validators and production-rooted incident corpora.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an emulator-validated generate→validate→repair pipeline to an LLM-only workflow using a deterministic harness and a single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini). All 120 paired episodes were emulator-valid in both conditions (n_11=120), yielding a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00]). Reviewer-requested clarifications grounded in archived artifacts are incorporated: the run used a shared initial generation per task (model_calls_used = 120), guarded repairs were conditional on validator-detected violations (none occurred; repair_applied = false), and key artifact filenames and archival manifest locations are referenced for reproducibility. The result is narrowly scoped: a ceiling effect on a synthetic, well-scoped task bank under a frozen prompt/model. To determine operational value of guarded workflows across realistic heterogeneity, future work must test independent-generation designs, multiple models/prompts, larger repair budgets, and higher-fidelity validators on production-rooted incident corpora.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the observed ceiling and limits inference about generation-induced failures.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but necessarily simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
